submission.natural_language_explanation: The negative pole of L13/N2052 is a Wikipedia category-markup detector: it fires when the text contains a wiki category declaration ('Category:<term>', and even more strongly '[[Category:<term>]]'), ramping through 'Category' and ':' to a peak on the opening tokens of the category term, and it fires hardest when that term begins with a 4-digit year ('Category:1903 births/films', peak ~2.0 locally and 3.4 in full articles), less for word terms ('Category:Italian cyclists' ~1.4) and single words ('Category:Physics' ~0.9). The trigger is the wiki category syntax plus a year-like value, not the tokens or the year itself: running prose ('He was born in 1903', 0.2), ordinary label lines ('Name: John Smith' 0.07, 'Year: 1903 births' 0.46), CSV rows and infobox fields stay near zero, and a minority of strong activations (5 of the 20 scan examples, in non-wiki prose) are not explained by this hypothesis.
